If you're still on the fence about installing macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple’s massive batch of security patches might be enough to convince you. And if you're sticking with an older version, you should install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.7 as soon as possible. Here's why.

Apple patches over 200 macOS vulnerabilities

Apple today published its full security release notes for macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8, detailing over 200 vulnerabilities addressed in the updates.

As with recent macOS updates, Apple's credit list includes several AI-focused security teams and researchers, including OpenAI Codex Security, NVIDIA AI Red Team, and Anthropic Research.

The macOS 27 patches cover a wide range of flaws, including ones that could allow malicious apps or attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel or root privileges, escape the macOS sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper protections, modify protected system files, and access sensitive user data.

One vulnerability in AVEVideoEncoder allowed sandboxed apps to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges. Meanwhile, a UDF file system vulnerability could similarly allow apps to run code at the kernel level. Apple also fixed bugs that could lead to remote code execution via Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.

macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8 patch many of the same vulnerabilities, including some of the above flaws involving kernel-level code execution, root privileges, sandbox escapes, Gatekeeper bypasses, and remote code execution.

For older versions, there are also some additional fixes not included in macOS 27, such as an ImageIO vulnerability in macOS Sequoia 15.8 that could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a specially crafted malicious image.

  • About the security content of macOS Golden Gate 27
  • About the security content of macOS Tahoe 26.7
  • About the security content of macOS Sequoia 15.8

Will you upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate, or stick with macOS Tahoe 26? Let us know in the comments.
